## Cutoff race

`end_holdings` checks the store snapshot's `from < mergedAt`, then drops `from` when building `ReleaseTarget`; it retains only role, instance and seat. Under the directory writer lock, `release_many` selects the currently open holding with that tuple, without checking its start against the merge cutoff or selected incarnation.

Concrete interleaving: a delayed/repeated `delivered` selects an eligible old holding; another operation ends it and reassigns the same role/instance to the same seat after the merge; the delayed writer then ends the new holding. The store update receives that newly selected row, so it does not restore the earlier cutoff check.

Preserve the selected holding identity and recheck the actual matched row's start/cutoff under the writer lock. A concurrent reassignment regression is needed; the sequential replay test does not cover this interleaving. This is source-confirmed reasoning, not an executed reproduction or production-state claim.

## Source and documentation repairs

`mergedAt` comes from the same `gh pr view` response as merge state/commit, for the requested PR number in the resolved repository. No cutoff argument, PR-body value or file timestamp supplies it. Missing/unparseable merge time leaves holdings alone; missing/unparseable holding time does not select it; equality and later starts are excluded at snapshot time. The shared parser accepts bare dates and space-separated timestamps as well as RFC3339, so no strict RFC3339-only guarantee is claimed.

The API doc and PR body now explicitly name inherited F88/req-10 authority, paths not proving completion, and directory-write-only atomicity (`docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:1043-1048,1720-1730,1738-1741`). They do not claim deployed provenance or global Git/SQLite recovery. Those three documentation notes from the prior verdict are addressed; its other scoped qualifications remain.
